Diff 253 lines shows targeted declustering + distinct-sources revision only: header/status/footer to Scheduled re-verification Oct25 2026 execution 2026-10-23 note; Opening Situation declustered (Mx Rivera removed cane/extra time, added self-filled preference agency; Mr Jackson 62 with handwritten ASL preference; Aisha 17 peer volunteer with prior labeling agency; Ms Thompson 68 cane separate); §4 split into 4 names/pronouns [M03-2] and 4B language access Title VI [M03-6]; §5 distinct ADA [M03-7] + Ms Thompson agency; Examples 1-5 all rewritten with ask-vs-infer and agency; Chapter Recap expanded to 9 objective-linked lines; KCs 31-38 explanatory answers added; footer expanded. No unrelated files changed.

Characters have individual preferences and agency; clustering avoided: Mx Rivera (34 community health worker, self-filled form, stated they/them + Spanish interpreter + 'I want to follow along and ask questions myself' — 2 language/identity traits with agency, not 4), Mr Jackson (62 retired housing advocate, own words 'I can read English. I prefer ASL for detailed forms — I can write for scheduling' — age+deafness with stated preference), Aisha (17 peer volunteer, previously offered 'Can we list what's in dishes so everyone can choose? I can help label them' — hijab + youth volunteer + prior contribution, not just object of complaint), Ms Thompson (68 cane after knee surgery, stated 'I like to take my time at kiosk — extra minute' — mobility separate person). Each person stated what helps them; staff taught to ask and document stated preference, not infer from appearance (cane, hijab, surname, accent, age) — §§3-5 and all Examples explicitly state ask-vs-infer.

Language access, disability accommodations, respectful communication have distinct explanations and applicable sources: §4 Respectful Communication — names/pronouns/identity distinct from language need — source NYC CCHR Gender Guidance [M03-2] protecting gender identity/expression including pronouns in public accommodations; §4B Language Access — separate obligation under Title VI Civil Rights Act 1964 for federally funded programs, LEP.gov planning guidance [M03-6] (qualified interpreters, not family); §5 Disability — separate legal basis ADA Titles II/III effective communication reasonable modifications [M03-7] (ASL/Video Remote, captioning, large print, extra time). Each section cites distinct official source, explains different law/aid, and is practiced in separate Examples (1 for names/pronouns, 2 for language, 3+5 for disability, 4 for belonging). Distinctness stated explicitly in section headers ('distinct from language access', 'distinct legal basis: ADA').

Scenarios teach readers to ask what assistance someone wants rather than infer needs from appearance: §3 bias lesson 'Do not infer language need from surname/accent/appearance — ask what person prefers' [M03-6]; §4B Working with interpreter 'Offer early: Would you like one in Spanish? Do not infer from surname/accent' + 'Document person stated preference'; §5 Mobility 'Do not infer from cane that someone cannot use touchscreen — ask' + Ms Thompson stated preference followed; §5 Hearing 'Do not infer reading ability from Deaf identity, ask stated ASL vs written preference — Mr Jackson wrote it'; Example1 repair 'is that what you'd like today?' ask; Example2 ask preference first; Example3 ask which he wants today; Example5 ask what she wants; KCs 32-35 correct answers all require asking preference. No scenario infers need from appearance alone.
